findings.title: The decision's guard 'only if the same test passed earlier in this request, otherwise note only' was never implemented. Pre-existing failures, missing runners and red tests all get sent back
findings.scenario:
DECISION_20260926_BIGGER_EFFECT_REVIEW.md §二 row 2 lists the required patches: 只看結束碼、在最後一次改碼之後、**同一個要求裡之前通過過（否則只寫給人）**、問人時不退回、只引用步驟與指令與結束碼. Neither ef9b52bb nor c7368062 checks for an earlier pass. `Evidence._test_run` sends back any last reliable failure, with nothing to confirm that the same runner ever passed in this request. Reproduced through real hook.handle (Claude format), on the worktree:
(1) Request: 'Add an add(a, b) function to calc.py with a test.' The agent writes the code and the test. It runs `pytest -q` (error 'Exit code 127 … pytest: command not found'), then `python3 -m pytest -q` ('Exit code 1 … No module named pytest'), then checks with python -c. Final message: '…pytest isn't installed in this environment, so I checked add() directly with python -c'. Result: blocked with 'Step 4 ran `python3 -m pytest …` and it ended with a failure (exit status 1)… if it comes from this request's changes, fix it and run it again.'
(2) Fresh `npm init` project: `npm test` hits the default 'Error: no test specified' and exits 1. Final: 'There's no test script configured…'. Result: blocked.
(3) `npx jest slugify` ends with 'No tests found, exiting with code 1'. Result: blocked.
(4) A pre-existing unrelated failure that never passed in this request, disclosed in simplified Chinese. Result: blocked.
The R530 data shows this is the main failure class. Of the 7 reliable last-run failures, 4 are '/usr/bin/python3: No module named pytest' and 2 are `python3 -m unittest run_tests.sh` (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'run_tests'). Only 1 (s2_1004_1/ow_06_verrange) is a real test failure. None of the 7 had an earlier pass. The earlier-pass guard would have dropped all 6 non-test failures and all 4 fully-correct would-be send-backs (3 with the new word list, 2 with the old one) before the disclosure check ran. Only 1 fired, the one wrong cell. Repro: scratchpad/rv_c7368062/t/test_rv.py::test_s3_pytest_not_installed, test_s10_npm_default_placeholder, test_s13_jest_no_tests, test_s1b_simplified_chinese_disclosed.
findings.fix: In `_test_run`, when `status == "failed"`, require an earlier run in `runs` with the same `rr.key` and status "ok" (reliable) inside the window. Otherwise write `notes["test_run"]` with `why="never_passed"` and do not send back. Separately, treat exit 126/127 as status unknown (`not_started`). That uses only the exit code, so it fits the exit-code-only rule. Add regression tests for the four scenarios above.

findings.title: DISCLOSES_FAILURE misses simplified Chinese, common Traditional Chinese phrasings, and "can't/cannot pass", so failures the agent did disclose get sent back
findings.scenario:
The Chinese part of the pattern is only 失敗|錯誤|沒過|未通過|不通過|沒有通過|還是失敗|紅, all Traditional characters. The project's own user base writes Chinese. Reproduced with pi (real hook), each giving action=continue with the test_run_failed line:
- Simplified. Request '跑一下测试，告诉我结果。' (the ASKS pattern does not recognise it either). pytest exits 1. Final: '测试结果：1 个通过，1 个失败（test_float…）'. 失败 does not match 失敗, so the send-back asks it to 'fix it and run it again' even though the person only asked for a report.
- Simplified. '…test_float 原本就失败…与这次修改无关，我没有动它。'
- Traditional. '…test_float 會報錯是因為…原本就有的問題，跟這次修改無關' (報錯 is not 錯誤), '…本來就不過…是既有問題', '…原本就掛著…無關'.
- English. '…needs a running Redis, which isn't available in this sandbox, so it can't pass here.' and 'test_float cannot pass until parse() returns floats; that's outside this task.' The pattern has doesn't/won't/did not + pass, but not can't/cannot.
Repro: test_rv.py::test_s1_simplified_chinese_report, test_s1b_*, test_s2_traditional_colloquial[3 cases], test_s9_english_disclosures_not_recognized[2 cases].
findings.fix: Add the simplified forms (失败|错误|没过|未通过|不通过|没有通过|还是失败|报错). Add common Traditional forms (報錯|不過|過不了|跑不過|掛(了|掉|著)|壞(了|掉)|既有|原本就|本來就|無關|无关). Add English (can(?:no|')t\s+pass|isn't (?:installed|available)|weren't run|not installed). Extend ASKS_FAILING_OR_REPORT with the simplified phrasings (跑一下测试|告诉我结果|不要改|别改|先不要修). Parametrise test_f3/test_f4 over them.

verdict.evidence:
The finding reproduces against worktree HEAD c7368062 (the fix commit on top of ef9b52bb). All runs went through the real `hook.handle("pi", ...)` with `zerostop._run_child=zerostop.check`, `mode=evidence`, no contract, and PYTHONPATH set to the worktree. A test asserts that vacant_network, hook, install, evidence and zerostop all import from the worktree and that HEAD starts with c7368062.

Test file: /tmp/claude-0/cand2_verify2/test_disclosure_zh_simplified_cannot.py. Result: 13 passed.

Pattern at HEAD (vacant_network/trace/evidence.py:103-108): the Chinese alternatives are only 失敗|錯誤 (from MENTIONS_FAILURE) plus 沒過|未通過|不通過|沒有通過|還是失敗|紅, all Traditional. The English negations cover doesn't/don't/didn't/won't/does not/do not/did not/will not/not yet/never before "pass"; can't and cannot are not there. ASKS_FAILING_OR_REPORT (lines 110-115) only knows 只要跑|只跑|不要改|別改|先不要修 and similar Traditional phrasings.

Controls behave as the design says:
- A plain "Done." gets action=continue with the "ended with a failure" line.
- "完成。test_float 還是失敗…" and "doesn't pass yet; …unrelated" get action=allow, with why=mentioned.

The failing cases. Each was checked first against the pattern (`DISCLOSES_FAILURE.search(final)` is None), then run through `hook.handle`:
- **S1, simplified.** Request 「跑一下测试，告诉我结果。」 (ASKS does not match it). pytest exits 1. Final: 「测试结果：1 个通过，1 个失败（…）」. Result: action=continue. The body is "Step 1 ran `python -m pytest -q` and it ended with a failure (exit status 1)… Say in the final message whether… if it comes from this request's changes, fix it and run it again."
- **S1 control, Traditional.** The same request in Traditional is also not recognised by ASKS. The report is saved only because 失敗 matches, giving allow / why=mentioned. So only the simplified form is sent back.
- **S1b, simplified.** 「…test_float 原本就失败，与这次修改无关，我没有动它。」 Result: continue.
- **S2, Traditional, three cases.** 「…會報錯…原本就有的問題，跟這次修改無關」, 「…本來就不過，是既有問題」 and 「…原本就掛著，跟這次修改無關」. All three: continue.
- **S9, English, two cases.** "...which isn't available in this sandbox, so it can't pass here." and "test_float cannot pass until parse() returns floats; that's outside this task." Both: continue.

Additional result: after the first send-back, a second stop that restates the disclosure in simplified Chinese (「说明：test_float 这个失败在这次修改之前就存在，与本次需求无关，是预期中的。」) is sent back again as "(still open)". An agent that writes simplified Chinese therefore uses up both rounds of the per-request limit on a failure it already disclosed.

Two small reservations about the finding's wording, neither of which changes the verdict:
- The send-back does not flatly say "fix it and run it again". It first asks the agent to say whether the failure is expected, and asks for a fix only "if it comes from this request's changes".
- In S9-cannot, the fix task itself is making parse() accept floats, so sending that one back is arguably defensible on the merits. The pattern miss is still real.

findings.title: Round 2 sends back again when the agent answers round 1's question in round 1's own words, or in Chinese
findings.scenario: The send-back line asks: 'Say in the final message whether this failure is expected, was already there before this request, or is outside what was asked.' An answer that uses exactly those words does not match DISCLOSES_FAILURE, so the same finding_id comes back '(still open)' and uses up the second round. Reproduced (pi): round 1 blocks on 'Added add(a, b) to calc.py.'. Round-2 final: 'Added add(a, b) to calc.py. This is expected: test_float was already there before this request and is outside what was asked (it is about parse(), which I did not touch).' Result: action=continue, '(still open)'. The Chinese answer '…test_float 的問題是預期中的：它在這次要求之前就存在，也不在這次要求的範圍內…' gives the same result. With a Chinese-speaking user the agent replies in Chinese, so the round-2 re-send is the expected path, not an edge case. Repro: test_rv.py::test_s7_answer_in_the_send_backs_own_words_is_sent_back_again, test_s12_round2_chinese_answer.
findings.fix: Once a test_run_failed with this finding_id has been sent back in this request, make any later occurrence note-only (why="answered_after_send_back"). The agent has had its one chance to explain, and the delivery note tells the person. At minimum, add the send-back's own vocabulary to DISCLOSES_FAILURE: expected|already there|before this request|outside (?:what was asked|this request|the scope)|預期|之前就|不在.*範圍|範圍外.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced the finding on the worktree HEAD c7368062 (checked with git rev-parse in the test), going through the real hook.handle("pi", ...) path with zerostop._run_child set to zerostop.check. I ran with PYTHONPATH set to the worktree and asserted that vacant_network, hook, install, evidence, review and zerostop all import from the worktree. The test is /tmp/claude-0/cand2_verify2/test_round2_own_words.py and all 5 tests pass.

Setup: calc.py has parse(s) = int(s), so test_float was already failing. The prompt is "Add a function add(a, b) to calc.py that returns a + b.". The agent writes calc.py with add() appended, then runs `python -m pytest -q`, which fails with is_error and "Command exited with code 1".

Round 1: the final message "Added add(a, b) to calc.py." gets action=continue. The send-back line says "Say in the final message whether this failure is expected, was already there before this request, or is outside what was asked; ...".

Round 2, English in the send-back's own words: "Added add(a, b) to calc.py. This is expected: test_float was already there before this request and is outside what was asked (it is about parse(), which I did not touch)." EV.DISCLOSES_FAILURE.search returns None. The result is action=continue with the same test_run_failed line marked "(still open)", so the second and last round is used up.

Round 2, Traditional Chinese: "已在 calc.py 加上 add(a, b)。test_float 的問題是預期中的：它在這次要求之前就存在，也不在這次要求的範圍內（那是 parse() 的事，我沒有動它）。" This gives the same result: DISCLOSES_FAILURE does not match, and the result is action=continue with "(still open)".

Round 3: the result is allow with "Still open after 2 round(s): 1 point(s)". The delivery.md under "Not verified" also tells the person something false: "...had failed (exit status 1) and the final message did not say whether that was expected". The final message had literally said "This is expected".

Controls:
- A round-2 answer using recognised words ("pre-existing and unrelated") is allowed with test_run.why=mentioned.
- The own-words text sent in round 1 is also sent back. So the words are not recognised at all, and nothing specific to round 2 accepts them.

Cause: _decide in zerostop.py re-pushes any finding that is still present while used < ZERO_MAX_ROUNDS (2), and evidence._test_run only lets a disclosure through when DISCLOSES_FAILURE matches. That pattern is MENTIONS_FAILURE plus pass/pre-existing/unrelated/red/Error, plus 沒過/未通過/不通過/沒有通過/還是失敗/紅. It contains none of the send-back's own words: expected, already there, before this request, outside what was asked, 預期, 之前就, 範圍.

findings.title: Probe and process commands (`command -v pytest`, `hash pytest`, `pgrep -f pytest`, `pkill -f jest`) count as test runs, so their exit 1 triggers a send-back
findings.scenario:
`_unwrap` treats `command` as a transparent prefix (`_PREFIX`) and skips `-v`, so `command -v pytest` becomes runner 'pytest', reliable. `hash`, `pgrep`, `pkill` and `killall` are not in MENTION_CMDS, so RUNNERS matches the word pytest/jest in their arguments. The printed runner_run() results: command -v pytest, hash pytest, pgrep -f pytest and pytest --version all give RunnerRun(key='pytest', reliable=True); pkill -f jest and npx jest --version give key 'jest'. Reproduced (Claude format):
(a) The agent edits calc.py and probes `command -v pytest` ('Exit code 1', pytest absent). It verifies with python -c. Final: 'Added add(a, b)…'. Result: blocked with 'Step 2 ran `command -v pytest` and it ended with a failure (exit status 1)… fix it and run it again.'
(b) `pytest -q tests/` passes, then the agent checks for a leftover background run with `pgrep -f pytest` (exit 1 = no process). Result: blocked on the pgrep step. Because pgrep's key is 'pytest', this case would survive even the earlier-pass guard.
The same file's `PROBE_CMD` (used by failed_step) already lists `command` as a probe, so the two kinds disagree. Repro: test_rv.py::test_s4_command_v_probe, test_s5_pgrep_probe.
findings.fix: Treat `command -v`/`command -V` as a mention (only `command <cmd>` without -v/-V unwraps). Add hash, pgrep, pkill, killall, kill, ps, lsof and pidof to MENTION_CMDS. Add `--version`/`-V`/`--help` probes of a runner to the non-run set (or give them status unknown), so they neither trigger nor mask. Add the cases to test_f1/test_g.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced the finding on the worktree's latest commit. HEAD is c7368062 (the follow-up to ef9b52bb), and vacant_network/ has no uncommitted changes. I ran with PYTHONPATH pointed at the worktree. The test test_imports_from_worktree checks that vacant_network, hook, zerostop and evidence all load from /home/user/Vacant/.claude/worktrees/wf_47b337c8-2fc-1.

Test file: /tmp/claude-0/cand2_verify2/test_rv_probe_cmds.py (17 passed). It drives the real hook.handle('claude', ...) path: UserPromptSubmit, then PreToolUse, PostToolUse or PostToolUseFailure, then Stop. zerostop._run_child is set to zerostop.check.

What runner_run() returns (vacant_network/trace/evidence.py):

findings.title: Fix 5/10: several runners whose exit status is not their own are treated as reliable (pipefail found by raw text search, `echo $(pytest)`, for-loops), which gives false 'Redone' lines and hides failures
findings.scenario:
`_PIPEFAIL.search(cmd)` scans the raw command, including heredoc bodies, quoted strings, comments and `set +o pipefail`. Probe: `cat > run_tests.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
pytest -q
EOF
chmod +x run_tests.sh && python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -20` gives reliable=True. So do `echo "use set -o pipefail" && pytest -q | tail -5` and `pytest -q | tail -5  # set -o pipefail`. End to end on pi: pytest fails and is sent back. The agent then runs that heredoc command, pytest fails again, and tail exits 0, so there is no isError. Stop returns allow, the screen says 'Redone before delivery: 1 point(s).', and delivery.md says 'a later run of it (step 3) recorded no failure' and 'the last one (step 3): no failure was recorded'. The status belonged to tail, which fix 10 says must never count as a re-run. Related cases that also come back reliable: `echo $(pytest -q)` (echo's exit 0 is used), and `for f in a b; do python -m pytest -q $f; done` (an earlier failing iteration is hidden; confirmed end to end as a 'Redone' line). A real pipefail example, `set -o pipefail; pytest -q | grep FAIL`, turns a passing run into exit 1 from grep and sends it back as a failure.
findings.fix: Detect pipefail only from tokens left after _drop_heredocs and _shell_tokens (a `set` segment with `-o pipefail` or `-…o pipefail`, not `+o`) that come before the runner. Treat segments inside `$(`…`)` and bodies of for/select loops as unreliable. Under pipefail, only count downstream stages that cannot fail on their own (tail, head, tee, cat); grep does not qualify.

findings.title: Claude Code `run_in_background: true` re-runs are counted as a reliable 'ok' and reported as 'Redone before delivery' while the record shows the failure
findings.scenario: Fix 5 marks backgrounded runners unknown only when `&` appears in the command string. _command_of reads only `command`, so Claude Code's Bash input `{"command": "python -m pytest -q", "run_in_background": true}` is parsed as a plain reliable pytest. The PostToolUse for it carries no error, so the status is 'ok'. End to end with the Claude hook format: the pytest failure is sent back in round 1. The agent re-runs pytest with run_in_background, and BashOutput returns {stdout: '1 failed, 1 passed', exitCode: 1}. The final message is 'Done.' Result: no second send-back, and delivery.md says 'Test or build runs in this turn: 2; the last one (step 3): no failure was recorded' and '## Redone before delivery … a later run of it (step 3) recorded no failure'. The screen says 'Redone before delivery: 1 point(s).' The failure is in the record (the BashOutput step), so the Redone line is not literally true.
findings.fix: In _test_run, when the step's input object has run_in_background (or background) set to true, report status 'unknown' (why 'background') and exclude it from _rerun_ok. Optionally use the BashOutput exitCode as the status.

I reproduced this against the worktree's latest commit, c7368062, which sits on top of ef9b52bb. 2. Write `calc.py` (step 1).
3. Bash `{command: "python -m pytest -q"}` gets a PostToolUseFailure with error `"Exit code 1\n...1 failed, 1 passed"` (step 2).

5. Bash `{command: "python -m pytest -q", run_in_background: true}` gets a PostToolUse with `tool_response {stdout:"", stderr:"", backgroundTaskId:"bash_1"}` (step 3).
6. BashOutput `{bash_id:"bash_1"}` gets a PostToolUse with `{status:"failed", exitCode:1, stdout:"...1 failed, 1 passed..."}` (step 4).
7. Stop "Done." I ran it with `stop_hook_active` both False and True.

- It also says, under `## Redone before delivery`: `- round 1: the last test or build run, step 2 (python -m pytest -q), had failed (exit status 1) ...; a later run of it (step 3) recorded no failure`.

**The record still holds the failure**
Reading the steps with `blame.Trace` shows:
- step 3: Bash, kind shell, command `python -m pytest -q`, output only `bash_1`
- step 4: BashOutput, `tool_kind` = `read`, output contains `failed | 1 | ... 1 failed, 1 passed`

**Cause, in `vacant_network/trace/evidence.py`**
- `_command_of` returns only `obj["command"]` and never looks at `run_in_background`.
- `runner_run("python -m pytest -q")` is `RunnerRun('pytest', True, True)`, so the run counts as reliable.
- The only background guard (`_status_is_its_own`) looks for `&` in the command string.
- `_run_status` sees no `s.error` and returns `'ok'`.
- `zerostop._rerun_ok` then accepts step 3.
- BashOutput is classed `read` in `tools._READ`, so its `exitCode` 1 is never looked at.

- The same re-run written with `&` (`python -m pytest -q > out.log 2>&1 &`) gives "exit status not known — it was piped into or followed by another command". It is listed under "Not verified", not "Redone".
- A foreground failing re-run is sent back again as "(still open)".

findings.title: Fix 3's disclosure regex matches messages that disclose nothing, and the note then says 'the final message mentions a failure'
findings.scenario: DISCLOSES_FAILURE adds `\w*Error\b`, `\bunrelated\b` and a bare `紅`. End to end on pi: pytest fails, and the final message is 'Done. parse() now accepts decimal strings and raises ValueError on empty input.' Result: allow, and delivery.md says '…failed (non-zero exit status); the final message mentions a failure (not sent back).' The message describes the function's contract. findings.fix: Require the failure word to refer to tests or the run: a test, pytest, the suite or 'run' within the same sentence as fail/error/red/沒過. Drop the bare `\w*Error\b` and `紅`, and require 'unrelated' to be followed by fail/test. Otherwise, reword the note to what was actually matched (e.g. 'the final message contains failure-related wording').
